title: Willie Rosenblum's band and the wood block
summary: Sal tells of replacing Godfrey in a Jewish band and Willie Rosenblum's rhythm.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You know, Schlegel. I never did know him.

Yeah, he played trumpet, or a Jew band. So, Goppsen, they quit the band to go with Leslie George, see. So they got me to play. It was a rock band, you know, I got to cut the mustard there. I went and played the band, the Jew band, see, with Willie. Willie was playing the Tulane band, the old college boy, see, Tulane. Went to the Rose Bowl and all that stuff, man, with Bill Bank and all, see. And they got, take a solo, Willie. And Raymond was laughing, man. Because Raymond was there for a good ear, man, Raymond. Yeah. You can't really know if you got the ear. Who's that guy? I said, that's Willie. He's playing.

I said, oh, God. Gee. I was trying to play on the drum, he goes ruh-tututututu. I said, on the wood block, man. Da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da. He played, man. So Goppsen quit. And the next job with Father Goppsen on, with Leslie's band. He went to Zenga Theater, man. So I know. See, I made my openings.
